text:
jamie: Quick proposal — tie prefetch entries to the active lease_id instead of just prefix key. Rationale: prevents serving prefetched KV that belongs to a previous owner after prefix handoff. Sketch: store lease_id on each prefetch entry and validate on serve; on mismatch either revalidate or fall back to miss. Thoughts?
lee: Strong correctness win. My worry is churn — if leases flip often we'll keep re-prefetching the same prefixes.
sophia: Agree with lee. Could we add a small grace window (e.g. 50-200ms) during handoff where we still serve the old prefetch to avoid latency spikes? Then trigger async revalidation.
matt: Memory/CPU question: adding lease_id to entries is cheap (8-16 bytes) but revalidation work could be heavy under high QPS. Need estimated cost for worst-case churn.
ali: Alternative: publish a revalidation event on lease_transfer that only enqueues affected prefixes into a bounded revalidation queue, de-dup by prefix. That avoids immediate thundering herd.
jamie: Exactly what I had in mind — two parts: 1) attach lease_id to entries; 2) on lease change, mark affected entries stale and enqueue revalidation with batching & backoff. Quick config sketch:
```
# prefetch lease binding modes
prefetch.bind_mode = "lease"
prefetch.lease_grace_ms = 100
prefetch.revalidation_batch = 128
prefetch.revalidation_backoff_ms = 50
```
lee: Nice. If we keep grace_ms tunable we can find a sweet spot. Also add a metric for revalidation queue length so SRE can watch.
sophia: Metrics to add: `prefetch.revalidations_total`, `prefetch.revalidations_dropped`, `prefetch.served_stale_after_handoff` (percent). Also log when a serve used a lease-mismatched entry and whether grace window allowed it.
matt: For perf testing let's spike lease rotations in a canary region and measure CPU/latency with parameters {50,100,200}ms. I can run that. Owners: jamie (design/RFC), matt (bench), sophia (metrics), ali (implementation spike).
ali: One more corner: what about pinned prefixes? Product teams will pin hot prefixes and expect them to survive handoffs. We should have `prefetch.pin=true` that bypasses lease invalidation unless explicit eviction.
jamie: Good call — add pin override. Also we should document semantic guarantees clearly: lease-bound prefetch = safe to serve only if lease_id matches OR within grace window OR pinned.
deploy-bot: canary: prefetch-lease-bind v0.1 deployed to eu-west-1, no regressions during initial 30m. :thumbsup:
sophia: After canary we should run a long-tail experiment with synthetic churn and real workload to track both revalidations and end-to-end p95/p99.
lee: UX question: will internal debugging tools show lease_id on entries? Operators will need that to trace stale serves.
jamie: yes — plan to extend the debug dump and console to display lease_id, last_revalidated_ts, and pin flag. I'll include that in RFC.
matt: OK let's do the spike tomorrow. If bench looks good we can RFC->PR.
jamie: Thanks all — I'll write up the RFC with the config knobs, metrics, and canary playbook and post the link here when ready.
